correction_retraction_20260803: The 'verdict' below is RETRACTED; raw data (results.csv) stands. The question itself was wrong: in-guest RCB-preemption determinism is NOT an open research question and NOT the S1 crux -- it is a solved, shipping mechanism in reverie-ptrace/src/timer.rs (fire-early at target-AMD_EPYC_9D85_SKID_MARGIN=1000, timer.rs:68, then single-step to exact RCB count via attempt_single_step timer.rs:800 / single_step_with_clock timer.rs:547) and in mozilla rr. This host runs it; no PEBS needed, so leg2 is irrelevant. Leg3's 'single-step = DBI re-entrancy wall' is retracted as a blocker (dbi-preemption-in-process-reentrancy-blocker is JIT clean-call re-entrancy, not proof in-guest determinism is unachievable). The real in-guest question is COST, not achievability: syscall-preemption is the fast primary path, RCB-overflow a rare fallback; RECORD may ignore skid, REPLAY uses scx-sim (breakpoint at known RIP + branch count); the real delta is counter attribution, handled by tool-RCB bracketing. See ai_docs/unified-patching-backend-constructor-feasibility_20260803.md '## CORRECTION'.
question: Can an in-guest PMU retired-branch-overflow interrupt (guest fields its own signal, no external ptrace tracer) land the guest deterministically across identical runs, or is it provably the DBI in-process re-entrancy wall again?
verdict: [RETRACTED 2026-08-03 -- see correction_retraction_20260803; the raw data stands but this NO/blocked/DBI-wall conclusion is wrong] NO on this host: nondeterministic landing (9 distinct RIPs / skid 15-90 over 20 identical runs) via the only available (non-precise) path; PEBS precise sampling that would remove skid is unavailable (precise_ip>0 => EOPNOTSUPP); the software skid-correction requires guest self-single-step = the DBI re-entrancy dead-end.

host_pmu_facts.perf_event_paranoid_meaning: own-process perf_event_open(pid=0,cpu=-1) permitted; cross-process/system-wide constrained. Spike stays own-process so it runs unprivileged and does not touch the pmu-serial flock.
host_pmu_facts.K_note: measured via kprobe.c: 5 pinned per-task generic counters run full-time on one core, 6th+ go to PERF_EVENT_STATE_ERROR = 6 hardware PMCs minus 1 NMI-watchdog. NOT 16 (that is LBR stack depth). reverie uses 2 pinned counters/guest thread => ~2 fully-RCB-instrumented threads co-schedule per core before panic.
host_pmu_facts.amd_precise_facility: IBS (ibs_fetch/ibs_op present) = statistical sampling, not per-event precise-RIP capture; not what reverie set_timer_precise needs

spike.guest: single process, ASLR off (ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE + re-exec), pinned cpu3, deterministic loop of 5,000,000 iterations x 1 conditional branch
spike.counter: PERF_COUNT_HW_BRANCH_INSTRUCTIONS, pinned=1 (matches reverie perf.rs:210), sample_period=1,000,000, precise_ip=0 (forced by host max_precise=0)
spike.delivery: SIGRTMIN on overflow via O_ASYNC + F_SETSIG + F_SETOWN_EX(F_OWNER_TID); handler reads RIP from ucontext, exact counter value, and loop iteration

three_legs_of_the_no: leg1 FUNDAMENTAL: non-precise counter-overflow delivery is nondeterministic on any hardware (skid 15-90 measured); margin tuning cannot fix landing RIP
leg2 HOST-SCOPED (AMD/no-PEBS): precise_ip>0 = EOPNOTSUPP; the precise facility that removes skid is unavailable here; reverie set_timer_precise cannot run on this host

leg3 FUNDAMENTAL: the ptrace skid-correction (fire-early + single-step to exact count) requires the guest to self-single-step from its own handler = DBI in-process re-entrancy dead-end (dbi-preemption-in-process-reentrancy-blocker)
what_would_change_the_answer: re-run leg2 on an Intel host WITH PEBS (precise_ip>0 succeeds) to test whether precise delivery gives a deterministic landing RIP without single-stepping
even a precise-landing YES leaves leg3 (safe park+RPC / re-entrancy from an in-guest signal context) untested by this spike
